title: A cooperative outer product declares an invalid accumulation interpretation
evidence: A direct entry-block OpCooperativeVectorOuterProductAccumulateNV has a known signed/unsigned 32-bit literal Matrix Interpretation other than FLOAT16 (0) or FLOAT32 (1). These are the only two intrinsic choices in the pinned rule; their respective native accumulation properties remain unknown. Godot 4.7's compiler accepts other literal interpretations. CooperativeVectorNV or CooperativeVectorTrainingNV must also be declared. Godot 4.4 rejects ordinary GL_NV_cooperative_vector source; its compiler-error versions suppress these checks. Operation checks omit helpers/later blocks. Only Vulkan imported versions with no stored base or stage compilation errors are inspected. Presence does not prove execution. No device support, measured cost, memory safety or complete pipeline compatibility is inferred; no shader or pipeline is created.
suggestion: Choose FLOAT16 or FLOAT32 accumulation and prepare compatible storage; separately establish support for that accumulation type on the intended device/engine.
tradeoff: Changing the accumulation type changes precision and buffer representation; an enum change alone does not convert stored data.
expected_effect: Identify a declared intrinsic Vulkan shader restriction; no speedup is predicted.
verify_step: Regenerate/reimport and repeat the audit, then verify the intended workload and numerical results on the target engine/device.

title: An imported shader uses a non-SPIR-V extension declaration
evidence: An imported RDShaderFile version without stored base or stage compilation errors contains an OpExtension name that does not begin with SPV_. Vulkan-ValidationLayers rejects this namespace; non-SPIR-V source extensions belong in OpSourceExtension. Both checked Godot compilers accept GL_EXT_spirv_intrinsics that emit arbitrary OpExtension strings, including GL_ names and an empty name. The scanner requires the actual Vulkan driver, reads at most 256 bytes for a terminated printable ASCII name and retains at most 16 distinct invalid names per module. Long, unterminated and non-ASCII names are skipped. SPV_ names are not assumed valid, but their registry membership and device requirements are outside this rule. Imported presence does not prove execution; no shader or pipeline is created.
suggestion: Remove non-SPIR-V names from the intrinsics' extensions requirement and use the actual SPV_ extension required by the emitted instruction, if any. Declare GLSL source extensions through their proper source mechanism.
tradeoff: Changing a string alone does not establish support for an instruction or feature. Preserve the intended shader semantics and verify the correct extension's requirements on each target device.
expected_effect: Identify emitted extension declarations that violate Vulkan's SPIR-V extension namespace before intended module creation; no speedup is predicted.
verify_step: Reimport and repeat the audit, then test the intended shader and outputs on target Vulkan devices. This check is not a complete extension or SPIR-V validator.

title: An imported shader declares a capability forbidden by Vulkan
evidence: An imported RDShaderFile version without stored base or stage compilation errors declares at least one of Addresses, Linkage, Kernel, Vector16, Float16Buffer, AtomicStorage or GenericPointer. These seven SPIR-V 1.0 capabilities are absent from Vulkan-ValidationLayers' allowed Vulkan capability table and have no enabling extension in the checked SPIR-V grammar. Both checked Godot compilers accept GL_EXT_spirv_intrinsics declarations that emit them, so compiler-error reporting alone misses this case. Offenders name the capabilities, resource version and shader stage. The audit requires the actual Vulkan driver and inspects stored bytecode; other capabilities, hardware-dependent requirements, other drivers and compiler-error versions are excluded. Imported presence does not prove execution, and no shader or pipeline is created.
suggestion: Remove the forbidden capability requirements or select a Vulkan-compatible shader variant. For address-based code, use the separately supported PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses feature rather than the Addresses or GenericPointer capabilities; preserve buffer layouts and caller bindings.
tradeoff: Removing a declaration is safe only if the instructions, types and storage classes it enables are also removed or replaced. A compatible implementation may change memory access or resource bindings.
expected_effect: Identify stored shader declarations that cannot be used in a Vulkan shader module; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: Reimport and repeat the audit, then test the intended shader and outputs on target Vulkan devices. The audit is not a complete SPIR-V validator.

title: An imported shader declares an 8-bit input or output
evidence: An imported RDShaderFile version with no stored base or stage compilation errors contains a typed OpVariable in Input or Output storage with an 8-bit integer or floating-point element. Vulkan forbids these objects unconditionally. Both checked Godot compilers accept scalar int8_t vertex/fragment inputs and outputs and retain the 8-bit declarations in SPIR-V, so compiler-error reporting alone does not cover this case. Every inspected public shader stage is considered. Numeric scalar/vector/matrix/array/struct type chains are inspected within 16 levels with cached visits; nested pointers, untyped variables, unknown types and deeper branches are skipped. This does not classify 8-bit buffers, push constants, workgroup data or 16-bit interfaces as invalid. Imported presence does not prove linking or execution; no shader or pipeline is created by the audit.
suggestion: Use a permitted interface representation, normally 32-bit integers for these values, and convert to or from 8-bit data within the shader. Update both sides of a stage interface and vertex attribute formats or render-target outputs as appropriate, then reimport.
tradeoff: A wider interface can increase data size. Preserve signedness and the intended values; support for 16-bit interfaces depends on a separate device feature and is not established by this check.
expected_effect: Identify compiled declarations that violate Vulkan's 8-bit Input/Output restriction before an intended pipeline is created; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: Reimport and repeat the audit, then test the intended pipeline and outputs on target devices with compatible interface types.

title: An imported storage-image format is unsupported on this Vulkan device
evidence: An imported RDShaderFile version with no stored base or stage compilation errors declares a UniformConstant storage image with a known explicit SPIR-V ImageFormat and descriptor set/binding. The corresponding Godot DataFormat does not support TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_BIT for either optimal or linear tiling on the current Vulkan RenderingDevice. The exact SPIR-V/Vulkan format mapping and both native Godot driver tables are checked. Direct and fixed-array 1D/2D/3D/cube images are inspected within existing scan budgets; buffer/subpass images, formatless or unmapped formats and unknown array lengths are skipped. Native support queries are cached per format. This reads declarations and format support without creating an image, shader or pipeline; project presence does not prove binding or execution. Other device features, usage combinations and dimensions are not validated.
suggestion: Choose a storage-image format supported on each target device, then update both the shader format qualifier and its matching RenderingDevice texture/view format. Retain a fallback if devices require different formats; merely removing the format qualifier does not establish formatless access support.
tradeoff: Changing format can change precision, range, signedness, bandwidth and memory. Preserve the intended values and algorithm; support for a format alone does not validate the complete texture, binding or shader configuration.
expected_effect: Identify a declared format with no supported Godot Vulkan storage-image tiling path on this device; no measured performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: Reimport and repeat the audit on target devices, then test the intended image creation, bindings and rendered or computed output using the matching format.

title: An imported shader contains an invalid SPIR-V header
evidence: While using Vulkan, a nonempty imported RDShaderFile stage within the scan budget is shorter than the five-word SPIR-V header, has a byte length not divisible by four, or starts with the wrong SPIR-V magic word. Its version has no stored base or stage compilation error. Oversized modules, empty absent stages, byte-swapped modules, unsupported execution models and other skipped reflection cases are not called corrupt. This reads stored bytes without creating a shader or pipeline; project presence does not prove execution. Header success does not validate the rest of the module.
suggestion: Reimport the source shader and inspect the reported resource/version/stage. If another tool writes RDShaderSPIRV bytecode, fix that output and restore a correctly compiled resource; do not submit the malformed bytes to a RenderingDevice.

expected_effect: Identify malformed stored shader data before attempting to create a Vulkan shader; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: Reimport and repeat the audit, then test the intended shader from valid compiler output on target devices.

title: Imported vertex and fragment interfaces do not match
evidence: A successfully compiled imported RDShaderFile version contains only vertex and fragment bytecode. At an explicit Location/Component slot, its vertex output and fragment input disagree on numeric kind or bit width, or a known fragment input has no matching vertex output. Missing-output findings require complete supported vertex reflection; unknown or truncated declarations suppress them. Godot compiles the stages separately. If linked together these declarations violate Vulkan's interface type requirement; file presence does not prove pipeline creation or execution. Numeric 16/32/64-bit scalars, vectors, matrices, fixed arrays and structs with explicit variable/member locations are inspected within 16 type levels and 1024 component slots per stage. Integer signedness is ignored, matching upstream. A PerVertexKHR fragment input ignores exactly its outer per-vertex array wrapper for interface matching. Unknown lengths/types, grouped decorations, overlaps and excess slots are skipped. Array lengths require known unsigned 32-bit constants. Unused outputs, built-ins, tessellation and maintenance4-dependent vector-size rules are not inferred.
suggestion: Provide the intended vertex output at the reported fragment-input location/component and make both numeric kind and bit width agree, then reimport. Check all variants and callers that use the paired stages.
tradeoff: Changing interface types can alter interpolation, precision and interpretation. Fix both sides according to the intended data rather than inserting an arbitrary cast.
expected_effect: Avoid linking incompatible stage interfaces; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: Reimport and repeat the audit, then test the intended graphics pipeline and rendered output on target devices.

title: An imported shader stage exceeds this GPU's push-constant size
evidence: The maximum known push-constant member offset plus its fixed scalar/vector/matrix/array payload exceeds maxPushConstantsSize. Padding is omitted and nested structs or unknown sizes contribute nothing, so the byte count is a lower bound. Godot reflects the block and creates a push-constant range starting at zero. Read from the actual Vulkan device through RenderingDevice.LIMIT_MAX_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE. Descriptor totals span distinct set/binding pairs in each inspected stage, despite Godot's PER_UNIFORM_SET enum name. Fixed image/sampler arrays are counted; buffer arrays, buffer/subpass images and unresolved lengths are omitted. Unknown limits and non-Vulkan drivers are skipped. File presence does not prove execution, and this is not a captured validation message.
suggestion: Reduce the shader's declared resources or push-constant payload, or select a variant compatible with the target GPU. Update RDUniform bindings and push-constant callers together.
tradeoff: Moving data into buffers or splitting work into passes can add memory traffic, binding work or dispatches. Validate output before comparing performance.
expected_effect: Avoid shader resource requirements that exceed a device limit; no speedup is predicted.
verify_step: Reimport the shader and repeat the audit on each target Vulkan GPU, then test the actual workload.

tradeoff: Moving data into buffers or splitting work into passes can add memory traffic, binding work or dispatches. Validate output before comparing performance.
expected_effect: Avoid shader resource requirements that exceed a device limit; no speedup is predicted.
verify_step: Reimport the shader and repeat the audit on each target Vulkan GPU, then test the actual workload.
